50298291.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to basic fibroblast growth factor (unknown origin) using sugar chip immobilized compound by surface plasmon resonance method
50298291.references_previous: 20. Wako, M.; Saito, A.; Ohshima, K.; Kishimoto, Y.; Nishimura, T.; Sobel, M.; Suda, Y. Bioorg. Med. Chem. Lett. 2008, 18, 2499. 21. Fukase, K.; Tanaka, H.; Torii, S.; Kusumoto, S. Tetrahedron Lett. 1990, 31, 389.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: After synthesizing the CS disaccharide library, the binding interactions of CS ligand conjugates were analyzed using an SPR imaging sensor. Ligand conjugates were immobilized onto gold chips according to a previous method. Basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) was chosen as a CS-binding protein; it strongly binds to the CS-E structure. As shown in Figure 2, the binding pattern varied depending on CS structure. Of CS disaccharides possessing mono- or disulfate groups like CS-A (GlcA-GalNAc4S), CS-C (GlcA-GalNAc6S), CS-D (GlcA2S-GalNAc6S), and/or CS-E (GlcA-GalNAc4S6S), which are the major forms occurring in nature, the CS-E and CS-D structures bound tightly to bFGF. CS disaccharides with minor disulfate patterns such as GlcA2S3S-GalNAc (CS-R), GlcA2S-GalNAc4S (CS-B), GlcA3S-GalNAc4S (CS-K), and GlcA3S-GalNAc6S (CS-L), also bound to bFGF with significant binding intensity. In addition, oversulfated disaccharides such as trisulfate and tetrasulfate, which are rarely found in nature, also bound tightly to bFGF. Although the effect of electrostatic interactions between oversulfated disaccharides and proteins should also be considered, the effect of structural interactions is important as evidenced by the variation in binding intensities observed for trisulfated disaccharides. The K_D values calculated using a 1:1 Langmuir binding model are summarized in Table 2 and K_D values on the nanomolar scale were observed in all cases. The SPR signal intensity depends on the protein binding level; however, no model has been proposed to estimate such a parameter. Detailed investigations are ongoing, but these results indicate that the structure-function relationship of CS with respect to GAG-binding proteins at the molecular level can be analyzed on-time by using our CS Sugar Chip.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Binding intensity with bFGF. Bar graph profiles of various protein concentrations. The error bars indicate SDs. Glc indicates Glcα1-4Glc ligand conjugate, used as a negative control.

The SPR signal intensity depends on the protein binding level; however, no model has been proposed to estimate such a parameter. Detailed investigations are ongoing, but these results indicate that the structure-function relationship of CS with respect to GAG-binding proteins at the molecular level can be analyzed on-time by using our CS Sugar Chip.

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: The binding properties of the synthesized CS disaccharide structures against basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) were evaluated by a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) imaging, indicating that our chip technology is effective for the evaluation of binding properties. The resulting ligand conjugates 39-54 were purified by ODS columns. After synthesizing the CS disaccharide library, the binding interactions of CS ligand conjugates were analyzed using an SPR imaging sensor. Ligand conjugates were immobilized onto gold chips according to a previous method. Basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) was chosen as a CS-binding protein; it strongly binds to the CS-E structure. As shown in Figure 2, the binding pattern varied depending on CS structure. Of CS disaccharides possessing mono- or disulfate groups like CS-A (GlcA-GalNAc4S), CS-C (GlcA-GalNAc6S), CS-D (GlcA2S-GalNAc6S), and/or CS-E (GlcA-GalNAc4S6S), which are the major forms occurring in nature, the CS-E and CS-D structures bound tightly to bFGF. CS disaccharides with minor disulfate patterns such as GlcA2S3S-GalNAc (CS-R), GlcA2S-GalNAc4S (CS-B), GlcA3S-GalNAc4S (CS-K), and GlcA3S-GalNAc6S (CS-L), also bound to bFGF with significant binding intensity. In addition, oversulfated disaccharides such as trisulfate and tetrasulfate, which are rarely found in nature, also bound tightly to bFGF. Although the effect of electrostatic interactions between oversulfated disaccharides and proteins should also be considered, the effect of structural interactions is important as evidenced by the variation in binding intensities observed for trisulfated disaccharides. The K_D values calculated using a 1:1 Langmuir binding model are summarized in Table 2 and K_D values on the nanomolar scale were observed in all cases. The SPR signal intensity depends on the protein binding level; however, no model has been proposed to estimate such a parameter. Detailed investigations are ongoing, but these results indicate that the structure-function relationship of CS with respect to GAG-binding proteins at the molecular level can be analyzed on-time by using our CS Sugar Chip.
